s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive ataxia with spasms and myoclonus
key_facts: Difficulty with gait progressed after cessation of alcohol use
Throat spasms do not affect speech or eating
Normal genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12
Severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI brain without contrast

shortlist.label: Multiple system atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction, and parkinsonism

shortlist.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Palatal myoclonus at 1-2 Hz, consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, myoclonus, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy

shortlist.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive ataxia and myoclonus, although less likely given the 20-year history

shortlist.label: Corticobasal degeneration
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, and rigidity, although less common

shortlist.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, bradykinesia, and supranuclear gaze palsy, although less likely given the absence of gaze palsy

shortlist.label: Friedreich ataxia
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive ataxia, although less likely given the late onset and absence of other characteristic features

raw.rationale: The combination of progressive ataxia, autonomic dysfunction (implied by the progression of gait difficulty after cessation of alcohol use), bradykinesia, mild rigidity, and severe cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on MRI is most consistent with Multiple system atrophy. The presence of palatal myoclonus also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Spinocerebellar ataxia type 7
rejected.why: Genetic testing for spinocerebellar ataxia types 1, 2, 3, 6, and 12 was normal, and while type 7 was not explicitly tested, the broader clinical presentation is more suggestive of Multiple system atrophy

rejected.label: Palatal myoclonus syndrome
rejected.why: While palatal myoclonus is present, it is part of a broader neurological decline, suggesting a more complex disorder like Multiple system atrophy

rejected.label: Dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and lack of specific mention of choreoathetosis or other characteristic features make this less likely

rejected.label: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease
rejected.why: The slow progression over 20 years does not fit the typically rapid progression of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease

rejected.label: Corticobasal degeneration
rejected.why: The absence of characteristic alien limb phenomenon or significant asymmetric parkinsonism makes this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: The presence of hypometric saccades could suggest this, but the overall clinical picture and severe cerebellar atrophy point more towards Multiple system atrophy

rejected.label: Friedreich ataxia
rejected.why: Typically presents earlier in life and with specific features like pes cavus and diabetes, which are not mentioned in the vignette
